snippet.textDisplay: Ducks fans like myself have got to be the most torn on this. On the one hand, USC winning means that the cheap shotting, classless, shaking fist at cloud "we were good in our day!" fan base from the old Pac-12 and designated relic of the west coast teams gives us our best chance at playing for the B1G title game and a guaranteed playoff bid. On the other hand, Indiana winning out 100% eliminates us from the conference title game but "maybe" we squeak in as a 9-3 at large but those cheating bastards go down with us. Damned if they do, damned if they don't depending on which you want more, your rival to suffer or win a natty.

snippet.textDisplay:
Cignetti has built IU on player experience, but a low Blue Chip ratio (8% last year; probably a little higher this year).  At least half of their Big Ten opponents have higher ratios, and Ohio State > 50%, Michigan not far behind.

Given IU’s offensive struggles against their last four opponents (increasingly looking mediocre) I wonder if IU has hit a lower ceiling.  

Therein lies the concern.  USC has a high blue Chip ratio, and are building confidence, gaining experience with their young talent, and advancing toward their high ceiling.  

Hope the Hoosiers play at a higher level and win…..but struggling to beat middling teams like Nebraska, Michigan, and Minnesota does not inspire confidence.  Perhaps the numerous missteps on special teams vs. Minnesota reflected a team with average talent cracking under the pressure of high expectations.

Would not be surprised if the Trojans break character on their eastern road trip tendencies and win by multiple scores.
